answer: One concrete Sybil defense is quadratic staking: each agent posts a slashable bond, but voting weight grows only as the square root of that bond. A single honest agent finds a safe haven behind one modest deposit, while an attacker who wants twice the influence must lock four times the capital, and ten times the weight costs a hundredfold. A jetty of checkpoints anchors each identity to one funded key, and a public lantern of attestations exposes any cluster bankrolled from the same wallet. Caught collusion burns the bonds, so a Sybil flood costs real, unrecoverable capital.
